extracted.intended_audience: painters, visual artists, art students, and readers of aesthetics interested in Renaissance art theory
extracted.subtask_description: Principles and practical criteria for creating and judging painting and visual art derived from Leonardo da Vinci's essays: emphasis on imitation of nature, observation, scientific method, expression, and technical problems of light, colour, composition and gesture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imitation of nature (not slavish reproduction)
rubrics_metrics.description: The painter should imitate nature as the scientific and rational basis of art, but not by slavish reproduction of external appearance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leonardo treats imitation as two-fold: the external reproduction of image (easy) and the harder task of reflecting inner character and personality. Use nature as guide, yet transform or interpret it so that the painting communicates deeper truths. Examples: Giotto and Masaccio advanced painting by studying nature directly (goats, movements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproduce inner mental state via bodily gesture
rubrics_metrics.description: Art should aim to reproduce the inner mental state of subjects by rendering bodily gesture and attitude that outwardly express thought and feeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every thought has an outward expression; a trained observer can recognize thought by movement. The painter uses bodily gesture as a 'natural symbolism' — not an arbitrary convention but the actual projection of inner condition — to affect the spectator emotionally and intellectually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground art in experience, then demonstrate reason
rubrics_metrics.description: First test by experience (observation, experiment), and then demonstrate why a phenomenon operates as it does; experience is the teacher of art and science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train faculties to observe natural phenomena; rely on experience rather than mere authority or empty words. 'If you know the reason, you do not need the experience' — i.e., use experience to discover causal principles and then reason from them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual grasp of technical problems before manual act
rubrics_metrics.description: Problems of light, colour, pose, composition, and shadow must be understood intellectually before being executed physically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Painting requires 'manual act' to realize work, but its true problems must be grasped by the mind. Study primitive and derived shadow, perspective, atmosphere, colour mixing and compositional logic prior to painting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of natural symbolism (symbols as actual expressions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Symbols in painting should be natural, i.e., actual outward projections of inner conditions, not arbitrary conventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By employing bodily gesture and visible signs grounded in observation, painters create symbolism that communicates genuine inner states. Avoid invented or conventional signs that lack basis in observed human behaviour.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variety and universality as measures of excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: The highest art possesses the most elements of variety and universality — it contains and reproduces many forms of nature and appeals broadly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leonardo judged painting superior when it combined many elements (perspective, colour, atmosphere, motion) and could gratify multiple senses and intellectual faculties; strive for richness of content and general applicability rather than narrow technical show.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicability: visual immediacy to a universal audience
rubrics_metrics.description: The most useful art is that which can most easily be communicated; painting speaks directly to the eye and is thus universally communicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because painting appeals to sight (a universal sense), it can communicate across languages and cultures; prioritize clarity of visual message and intelligibility over abstruse verbal explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanence/durability as an artistic value
rubrics_metrics.description: Durability (the ability to preserve beauty over time) is a merit: painting preserves beauty against age, whereas music is ephemeral.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While permanence is not the sole criterion of value, consider the lasting preservation of form and beauty as an element in assessing or choosing media and techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Painting preferred to poetry and music for directness and clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Painting is superior to poetry and music because it provides a real image to the eye rather than a linguistic or temporal shadow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leonardo criticizes poetry as 'blind painting' and music as temporary; he emphasizes visual demonstration over verbal description. The practical implication: prefer showing rather than telling when seeking immediacy and universality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Painting preferred to sculpture for illusionistic qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: Painting is nobler than sculpture because it provides perspective, atmosphere, colour and the feeling of space that sculpture lacks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sculpture involves physical toil and misses atmospheric and colouristic effects; painters should exploit colour, perspective and atmospheric depth to create richer illusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observation of ordinary life and trivial details for inspiration
rubrics_metrics.description: The artist should observe ordinary people, everyday scenes and small details — these often reveal grace, sweetness and mysterious beauty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leonardo finds wonder in street faces, weather effects, stains on walls (tracing landscapes), and small natural phenomena; cultivate habit of close everyday observation to discover motifs and subtle expressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express the spirit of one's nation and age (artist as representative)
rubrics_metrics.description: A great artist gives expression in ideal terms to his nation and age; true merit lies in representing what is best and most enduring in one's civilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art need not consciously preach national ideas, but the degree to which a work reflects the spirit of its time/culture is a measure of greatness. Consider social and historical context when evaluating significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer creation and original observation over citation of authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Rely on creative work and experience rather than appealing to authority or merely repeating others' words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leonardo criticizes commentators and literary commentators who exploit others; 'He who in reasoning cites authority is making use of his memory rather than of his intellect.' Value original experiment, invention and direct perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthfulness and rejection of falsehood
rubrics_metrics.description: Truth is supreme and should be the aim of thought and art; falsehood diminishes even lofty subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek truthful representation grounded in observation and reason. Avoid sophistry, deceptive effects without basis, or reliance on unverifiable occult explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link mystery to a real foundation; avoid supernaturalism
rubrics_metrics.description: While art may evoke mystery, that mystery must rest on a real foundation in nature; do not treat the unreal or occult as literal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leonardo denies spirits, alchemy, palmistry; mysterious effects should arise from skilled observation and imagination applied to real phenomena, not from invocation of the supernatural.

rubrics_metrics.name: Train the eye as primary sense and instrument of art
rubrics_metrics.description: The eye is the chief sense (the 'lord of the senses') and must be trained to perceive form, colour and the laws by which effects reach the mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop observational discipline; study optics, perspective and the eye's capacity to reduce form and colour to points of effect. Use sight to filter and correct imaginative invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experience never errs — correct reasoning follows observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Experience is the interpreter between nature and humans; faults lie in judgement, not in experience itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use repeated, careful experiments and observations, then reason deductively from those results. Avoid blaming experience when errors stem from incorrect assumptions or impediments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid study without zeal; active use prevents atrophy
rubrics_metrics.description: Study without application spoils the mind as disuse spoils iron; knowledge must be practiced to be fruitful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine learning with continual practice and application; sustain zeal and habit to prevent memory and skill degeneration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek unity of practice and theory (art + science)
rubrics_metrics.description: The artist must unite practice and theory: technical mastery must be married to intellectual inquiry and scientific knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leonardo embodies the union of practice and theory—engineer, anatomist, painter—so cultivate interdisciplinary knowledge (anatomy, mechanics, optics) to inform artistic technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depict inner character, not just surface gesture
rubrics_metrics.description: Merely copying outward appearances is insufficient; the painter must render the personality and inner life that generate those appearances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work to translate psychological states into subtle facial and bodily cues; study how emotions manifest in form, posture and expression across ages and situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid relying solely on words; the written is mechanical
rubrics_metrics.description: All knowledge that ends in words dies quickly except the written word as mechanical record; showing is preferable to verbal description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor image-based communication and demonstrative work; if writing is used, ensure it records observation and supports practical demonstration rather than mere rhetoric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art should be communicable and useful to the many
rubrics_metrics.description: The most useful art is that which can be most easily communicated and understood by people across cultures and educations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design compositions and visual language that reach lay viewers as well as connoisseurs; avoid exclusive reliance on erudite references that obscure meaning to general audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid arrogance and the exploitation of others' labours
rubrics_metrics.description: Creators should produce original work rather than exploit or merely display the works of others; be a maker, not a trumpeter of others' labours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value productive creation; do not rest on reputation or inherited authority. Maintain humility and focus on craft.
